kept.spine: Market day brings the town out of doors, and the stalls see trade enough to justify staying open.
A paid garrison and a professional watch answer for Rundgate's safety, not neighbours called up when trouble comes.
There is enough here that an argument about money is the rare one.
The town expects to keep being what it already is.
The walls are kept for use, not for looking at.
Enough armed men can be put on the walls here to matter, and they carry themselves like men who have done this before.
Children here are taught the rules about the dark early, and the rules are kept.
Here the watch answers what is reported to it and does not go looking beyond that.
Prices here hold steady, in a way that suggests the town is not living on the last thing it sold.
There is somebody here who can do what is usually asked of them and knows plainly what is beyond them.
Nobody here spends much thought on food, and that is the best any town's food can claim.
Passing trade off the road to somewhere else is how the town makes its modest living.
What the town cannot grow for itself, the road supplies, and the road is less a convenience here than a condition of living at all.
Size alone means some quarters here do not know each other.
The town's dealings with its neighbours show no strain that marks it out from anywhere else.
